FAQs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQs.subheading: Here are the most common questions about Odontis and how it works.
FAQs.a1: Dental caries is a tooth decay disease caused by bacteria that produce acids, which damage the outer protective layer (enamel) of the tooth.
FAQs.a2: Gum disease is an infection of the tissues supporting the teeth. The early stage is called gingivitis and the advanced stage is called periodontitis.
FAQs.q3: How many teeth do adults normally have?
FAQs.a3: A healthy adult typically has 32 permanent teeth, including incisors, canines, premolars, and molars.
FAQs.a4: A supernumerary tooth is an extra tooth beyond the normal number. It may cause crowding or misalignment of teeth.
FAQs.a5: Brush twice daily, floss once a day, limit sugary foods, drink plenty of water, and visit a dentist regularly.
FAQs.a6: Odontis does not provide any medical diagnosis. Always consult a qualified dental professional for proper treatment, as AI systems may make mistakes.
